reason: E2 confirms the dual-layer structure and graded hardness, supporting premises 1 and 2. E1 shows hardness and wear improvements from active screen nitriding, partially supporting premises 3 and 4, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence on fracture toughness retention, leaving premise 5 unsupported. The cited evidence is accurately represented but incomplete for the full set of claims.
premises: Active screen ion nitriding of TC4 produces a dual-layer nitride structure (δ-TiN/ε-Ti2N composite + α-Ti(N) diffusion zone).
This dual-layer structure creates a graded hardness profile that avoids abrupt property mismatch.
The graded structure improves wear resistance and mechanical integrity under high-contact stress.
Surface microhardness increases 2–3 times and wear volume reduces by over 80% relative to untreated TC4.
The treatment does not significantly compromise substrate fracture toughness.
